global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering, not a readership or download ranking. Citation evidence is limited for such recent papers and no citation momentum could be established.

sections.title: Quantum phase estimation on a Rydberg quantum simulator
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate phase-sensitive many-body spectroscopy on an analog Rydberg simulator, extracting absolute ground-state energies, gaps, and energy-filtered observables for systems of up to 19 atoms without auxiliary qubits or controlled evolution.
sections.claimed_result: The authors reconstruct the complex Loschmidt echo on a strontium-88 Rydberg platform and use its Fourier transform to recover ground-state energies and energy-resolved observables in 1D and 2D arrays.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; analog Rydberg simulator with up to 19 atoms, digital state preparation, native evolution, and phase reconstruction using short imaginary-time steps
sections.unique_caveat: The finite evolution-time window limits energy resolution, especially for smaller gaps; the phase protocol also uses an approximate imaginary-time implementation under the stated blockade model.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in quantum and atomic physics, the paper reports an experimental capability beyond ordinary gap spectroscopy; a third-party science summary appeared shortly after posting. This is an early discussion signal, not evidence of broad readership.

sections.title: Observation of $^{71}$Cr and expanded cross-section measurements and analysis of $^{82}$Se fragmentation
sections.abstract: The authors measure neutron-rich isotope production, including the first observation of $^{71}$Cr, and compare abrasion-ablation and binding-energy-systematics predictions across eleven nuclear mass models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a measured $^{71}$Cr production cross section of $2.20^{+2.10}_{-0.75}\times10^{-13}$ mb, consistent with the earlier $1.94\times10^{-13}$ mb prediction from the stated $\Delta BE_{\rm sys}$ coefficients and HFB-22 masses.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; $^{82}$Se fragmentation at FRIB/ARIS, event-by-event particle identification, and cross-section analysis with LISE++ and eleven mass models
sections.unique_caveat: The $^{71}$Cr cross-section uncertainty is large and asymmetric; predictions remain mass-model dependent, and the authors note that current reaction calculations underpredict some neutron-rich yields, possibly because of missing reaction mechanisms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A first isotope observation is paired with an out-of-sample test of a production-cross-section prediction made before the observation; the arXiv comment says the manuscript is to be submitted to Physical Review C.

sections.title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
sections.abstract: Using Super-Kamiokande phases I–IV, the authors infer solar-core bounds and temperature from the $^8$B neutrino spectrum, with a tighter radius bound when SNO coefficients are included.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 90%-confidence upper bounds on the core radius ranging from $0.499R_\odot$ to $0.381R_\odot$ in Super-K-only fits across the stated solar models, tightened to $0.268R_\odot$ and $0.215R_\odot$ in the corresponding Super-K-plus-SNO fits.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Super-Kamiokande phase I–IV recoil-electron spectra, with SNO polynomial coefficients in the combined analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The inferred radius varies with the adopted solar model and fit inputs, while the temperature estimate assumes nominal core size and density. The abstract gives a neutrino-production-zone temperature of $15.492\times10^6$ K, whereas the conclusion prints $14.492\times10^6$ K; that internal discrepancy needs clarification.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is cross-listed across particle physics and two astrophysics categories and analyzes 5,805 days of Super-Kamiokande data, with a combined fit using SNO information; these are complementary inputs in one analysis, not independent confirmations.

sections.title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?
sections.abstract: The authors jointly reconstruct the effective dark-energy density and gravitational responses to clustering and lensing from CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, and large-scale-structure data, finding a low-redshift background feature but inconclusive gravitational-sector behavior.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find a broad effective dark-energy-density maximum near $z\simeq0.6$–$0.7$; gravitational-response features are weaker and dataset-dependent, so the analysis does not establish a common physical origin.
sections.evidence_type: computational; non-parametric reconstruction and covariance-mode analysis of CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt, and other large-scale-structure observations
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that current data constrain the gravitational sector less precisely than the background and cannot determine whether the two apparent features share an origin.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The cross-list links cosmology and gravitation, and the joint use of CMB, DESI, supernova, and DES Year 3 large-scale-structure data makes this a concrete multi-probe reconstruction rather than a single-survey anomaly claim.

sections.title: Emerging understanding of the rare kaon decay $K^+\to\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$ from lattice QCD
sections.abstract: A near-physical-mass lattice-QCD calculation determines the sign of the vector form factor for a rare kaon decay and finds the negative-sign solution favored, with lower significance after extrapolation to physical charm mass.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find $V(0)<0$ with 5.8–7.9$\sigma$ statistical significance at charm mass $1.1$ GeV; after extrapolation to physical charm mass the negative sign persists at 2.0–3.4$\sigma$ across their fit forms.
sections.evidence_type: computational; first-principles lattice QCD using two domain-wall-fermion ensembles with near-physical pion masses and six momentum transfers
sections.unique_caveat: The physical-charm extrapolation weakens the significance to 2.0–3.4$\sigma$; the authors present the result as evidence favoring a sign, not a definitive high-significance determination at the physical point.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in lattice and phenomenological high-energy physics, the paper tackles a sign ambiguity that decay rates alone cannot resolve and checks the calculation with four independent subtraction schemes.

sections.title: What constrains the neutron-star crust? Present data, future measurements, and EOS doppelgängers
sections.abstract: A Bayesian study finds current crust constraints are driven mainly by chiral effective field theory, and forecasts that precise global stellar measurements may still fail to distinguish crust models with different internal properties.
sections.claimed_result: Within the adopted unified crust-core equation-of-state model, two models with nearly identical global observables can differ by about a factor of two in crust mass and crustal moment of inertia at the assumed precision.
sections.evidence_type: computational; Bayesian inference and forecasts using nuclear and astrophysical constraints with a unified crust-core equation of state
sections.unique_caveat: Results depend on the adopted theoretical bands, neutron-rich surface-energy treatment, and forecast reference equation of state; the analysis finds that global measurements alone do not uniquely determine crust properties.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The cross-list connects neutron-star astrophysics with nuclear theory, the manuscript is reported as submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics, and it quantifies a concrete degeneracy between global stellar observables and crust properties.
